Section A: Answer ALL the questions in the spaces provided (15 questions); the mark allocation for each question is indicated. Section B: Answer ALL FOUR questions in this section; all questions in Section B carry equal marks (15 marks each). You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. Duration: two and a half hours.

figures.legende: Figure 2: network with vertices A, B, C, D, E; edges AB, BC, BD, BE, plus curved edges AE, CD and DE.

incertitudes: Q8 : lecture de la Figure 2 - sommets A, B, C, D, E ; arêtes AB, BC, BD, BE, AE (courbe), CD (courbe), DE (courbe) ; 4 régions dont la région extérieure. Le calcul R+V-2=E donne bien 7.

questions.corrige_markdown:
The network divides the plane into: the region bounded by $A$, $B$, $E$; the region bounded by $B$, $E$, $D$; the region bounded by $B$, $D$, $C$; and the outside (unbounded) region.

**$R=4$.**

The edges (arcs joining two vertices) are $AB,\ BC,\ BD,\ BE,\ AE,\ CD,\ DE$.

**$E=7$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (d) Hence, show that $R+V-2=E$. *[6 marks for the whole question]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Left-hand side: $R+V-2=4+5-2=7$.

Right-hand side: $E=7$.

Both sides are equal, so $R+V-2=E$ is verified for this network (Euler's formula for networks).
